newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken says it forms new venture.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken says it forms new venture.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc said Friday it invested in a new company that will partner with Harry's Farmers Market Inc to capitalize on emerging trends in the food buying habits of consumers.

The new company, called Progressive Food Concepts Inc, will explore, with Boston Chicken, taking a line of Boston Market prepared foods into alternate distribution channels, potentially in partnership with supermarkets, Boston Chicken said.

Saad Nadhir is resigning as co-chairman and president of Boston Chicken to lead Progressive as chairman and CEO, working closely with Harry Blazer, chairman and CEO of Harry's, who will also serve on Progressive's board, Boston Chicken said.

Boston Chicken said the agreements between Progressive and Harry's include a $20 million investment from Progressive in the form of a loan to Harry's that can be exchanged for up to five million shares of Harry's Class A common stock, warrants to purchase two million shares of Harry's Class A common stock and a mutual consulting agreement between Harry's and Progressive.

In addition, Boston Chicken said, Progressive acquired Harry's worldwide intellectual property and trademark rights, including all rights to the Harry's Farmers Market and Harry's In A Hurry retail concepts.
Boston Chicken said Harry's will retain development and trademark rights to both concepts in Georgia and Alabama and will receive a 2.5 percent equity interest in Progressive.
Boston Chicken said there are no ongoing royalties or fees associated with the transfer of these rights.
Assuming full exercise of the rights to acquire Harry's stock, Progressive could own about 43 percent of Harry's, Boston Chicken said.
